stories.title: Hermit CRM – Free open-source CRM for solopreneurs
stories.body:
I was about to keep track of my clients and prospecting in Google Sheets for my solopreneur business, when I remembered that's exactly what I advise my clients not to do.

Created Hermit CRM, an open source CRM for 1 person. Hermit helps to keep track of deals and prospecting. The platform is built for AI by storing the data in Markdown files in git, stored locally and can be accessed with a web app, CLI or MCP. No telemetry on the app. Building in public, even the website stats are public as well.

It’s macOS first. Linux is less tested, and Windows isn’t supported.

Features I'm proud of: - import somebody from LinkedIn into to the CRM with 1 click - adding a LinkedIn convo to the CRM with 1 click. Both work without LinkedIn or CRM subs.

Don't like what you see? Fork the Hermit with your AI.

Would love to learn how you're using Hermit and where it doesn't fit your workflows.

discussion.author: dominotw

discussion.text:
A few extra details: Code: https://github.com/Hermit-CRM/hermit-crm

Why Markdown in git? So you can grep it, edit it in an editor, and an AI agent can read and update it without an API.

I use the MCP server a lot. I ask Claude things like "who haven't I followed up with in the last two weeks?".

Happy to implement what would make hermit-crm more useful for you.

Comp AI CRM is an open source, CRM designed for AI agents. Agentic-first CRM.

The agent · Stack · Quick start · Configuration · Deploying · Contributing

Most CRMs are a database with a form in front of it. The AI ones bolt a chat box onto the side of that form. Both leave the actual work — finding out what is true, and writing it down — to a human who has better things to do.

views.text: Personally I think anthropic, open AI and grok should all be shut down. What makes the AI actually dangerous is the millions of dollars of compute the frontier labs are willing to waste on their dangerous experiments. Most people do not have access to the hardware to make these models actually dangerous.

views.text: If you ever want a laugh, check out Anthropic's blog. Some of the posts are the red team dreaming up increasingly elaborate abuse scenarios for open weight models including a self-propagating open weight model that distributes its weights across IoT type devices like set top boxes and performs distributed inference. Stuff that is technically possible, and worth investigating as a research team, but so far from the most realistic harm AI could cause and does cause right now.
